newsitem.title: USA: Preferred Employers boosts IPO terms.
newsitem.headline: Preferred Employers boosts IPO terms.

text.p: Preferred Employers has boosted the terms of its proposed initial public offering, according to a filing with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission.

Preferred Employers now plans to offer 1.5 million shares of common stock in a range of $7 to $8 each. That means gross proceeds of the deal would be $11.25 million, slightly higher than its initial $9 million estimate.
In October, the company had estimated an offering of one million shares to price between $8 to $10 each.
The company provides workers' compensation and business insurance aimed at bringing lown claims costs at fast food restaurants and convenience stores.
Underwriter Commonwealth Associates was not immediately available for comment, but has said the offering is tentatively scheduled for early in February.
